analysis.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer remains a major global health challenge, especially in low- and middle-income countries, despite the availability of effective prophylactic human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines, screening methods and established treatments. The study aims to explore the current understanding of HPV genetic variation and virus-host interactions driving a shift from traditional prevention and treatment strategies to precision prevention and targeted therapeutics.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a review of current literature on HPV genetic diversity, viral persistence, and virus-host molecular interactions. It focuses on HPV-associated cervical cancer and other explicitly HPV-related diseases, including cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, HPV-associated anal cancer, and HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer.
analysis.methods: The study utilizes next-generation sequencing, molecular biomarkers, and artificial intelligence to refine risk stratification and therapy selection for HPV-associated diseases.
analysis.main_results: The study reports that HPV genotype distribution and differences in oncogenic potential inform vaccine development and screening strategies. It also highlights that molecular events such as viral insertion, epigenetic modifications, APOBEC-associated mutations, and immune escape contribute to disease progression.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the discoveries reveal molecular vulnerabilities that can be targeted therapeutically. This represents a novel approach to cervical cancer prevention and treatment by leveraging HPV genetic diversity and virus-host interactions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more precise prevention and treatment strategies for HPV-associated cervical cancer, potentially improving outcomes in affected populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a review and does not present original data, thus the evidence strength is moderate. The limitations include the reliance on existing literature and the absence of new experimental results.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of human papillomavirus (HPV) genetic diversity and virus-host interactions in cervical cancer prevention and treatment. It highlights the importance of HPV genotype distribution and oncogenic potential in shaping vaccine development and screening strategies. The study also discusses molecular mechanisms such as viral insertion, epigenetic modifications, APOBEC-associated mutations, and immune escape that contribute to disease progression. The authors emphasize the potential of targeting molecular vulnerabilities for therapeutic interventions. While the study provides valuable insights into the shift from traditional to precision approaches, it is limited by its reliance on existing literature and the absence of new experimental data. The findings have significant implications for improving surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment of HPV-associated cervical cancer, particularly in low- and middle-income countries.

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为针对 HPV 相关 宫颈癌 制定更精确的预防和 治疗 策略提供信息,从而有可能改善受影响人群的结果。

title_zh: 从 HPV 遗传多样性到精准治疗:病毒-宿主 相互作用以及 宫颈癌 预防和 治疗 的新兴策略
source_body_en: Cervical cancer is a major global health challenge, especially in low- and middle-income countries, despite the availability of effective prophylactic human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines, screening methods and established treatments. Cervical cancer is primarily caused by persistent infection with high-risk HPV, but persistent infection is necessary, but not sufficient, for the development of cancer. Advances in understanding HPV genetic diversity, viral persistence, and virus-host molecular interactions are creating new opportunities to improve precision in HPV prevention and treatment. HPV genotype distribution and differences in oncogenic potential inform vaccine development and screening strategies. The viral oncoproteins E6 and E7 disrupt host tumor-suppressor pathways, driving cellular immortalization and genomic instability. Molecular events such as viral insertion, epigenetic modifications, APOBEC-associated mutations, and immune escape contribute to disease progression. These discoveries have revealed molecular vulnerabilities that can be targeted therapeutically. Immune checkpoint inhibitors and antibody-drug conjugates are used clinically in specific contexts of cervical cancer presentation and treatment. At the same time, therapeutic vaccines, adoptive cellular immunotherapies, RNA interference, and genome editing are being investigated as complementary strategies to target HPV-associated cervical cancer. With advances in next-generation sequencing, molecular biomarkers, and artificial intelligence, these tools could further refine risk stratification and therapy selection. This review explores the current understanding of HPV genetic variation and virus-host interactions driving a shift from traditional prevention and treatment strategies to precision prevention and targeted therapeutics, and critically assesses remaining challenges.
abstract_zh: 尽管有有效的预防药物 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗、筛查方法和已建立的 治疗,宫颈癌 仍然是一项重大的全球健康挑战,特别是在低收入和中等收入国家。宫颈癌主要是由高危型HPV持续感染引起的,但持续感染对于癌症的发展是必要的,但还不够充分。在了解 HPV 遗传多样性、病毒持久性和病毒-宿主 分子相互作用方面取得的进展,为提高 HPV 预防和 治疗 的精确度创造了新的机会。HPV 基因型分布和致癌潜力的差异为 疫苗 的开发和筛查策略提供信息。病毒癌蛋白 E6 和 E7 破坏 宿主 肿瘤抑制途径,驱动细胞永生化和基因组不稳定。病毒插入、表观遗传修饰、APOBEC 相关 突变 和免疫逃逸等分子事件有助于疾病进展。这些发现揭示了可以作为治疗目标的分子漏洞。免疫检查点抑制剂和抗体药物偶联物在 宫颈癌 呈现和 治疗 的特定背景下临床使用。与此同时,正在研究治疗性 疫苗、过继性细胞免疫疗法、RNA 干扰和 基因组 编辑,作为针对 HPV 相关 宫颈癌 的补充策略。随着下一代测序、分子生物标志物和人工智能的进步,这些工具可以进一步完善风险分层和治疗选择。本综述探讨了目前对 HPV 遗传变异和病毒与 宿主 相互作用的理解,推动了从传统预防和 治疗 策略向精准预防和靶向治疗的转变,并严格评估了剩余的挑战。

title: [Radiotherapy of head and neck cancer : Highlights from the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting].
abstract: At the 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting, several studies focused on radiotherapy of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). The phase III AREST trial showed that adjuvant radiotherapy for early oral cavity cancer with intermediate-risk features can reduce the risk of locoregional recurrence. A post hoc analysis of the JCOG1008 trial found no increased locoregional recurrence rate even when adjuvant chemoradiotherapy was initiated later than recommended. Combined radioimmunotherapy (RIT) was also a major topic this year: in a subgroup analysis of the NIVOPOSTOP trial, the disease-free survival (DFS) benefit of nivolumab was maintained in patients with extensive neck dissection, which weakens the frequently highlighted mechanistic relevance of regional lymph nodes for the immune response. In the treatment of human papillomavirus (HPV)-positive oropharyngeal cancer, results for RIT were conflicting: the phase II CCTG HN.9 trial evaluating radiotherapy combined with durvalumab failed to meet its efficacy endpoint, whereas the phase II KEYCHAIN trial of definitive RIT with pembrolizumab demonstrated a significant improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) compared with cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy. In addition, a subgroup analysis of the combined positive score (CPS) ≥ 10 population of the KEYNOTE-412 trial underscored the importance of biomarker-based patient selection when combining radiotherapy and immunotherapy.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the role of human papillomaviruses (HPV) in the context of head and neck cancer, particularly in relation to radiotherapy and its impact on locoregional recurrence and survival outcomes. The central question is whether HPV-associated diseases, such as oropharyngeal cancer, benefit from specific radiotherapy approaches, including combined radioimmunotherapy.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on findings from the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting, including the phase III AREST trial, the post hoc analysis of the JCOG1008 trial, and subgroup analyses from the NIVOPOSTOP and KEYNOTE-412 trials. These studies were selected based on their relevance to HPV-associated diseases and their focus on radiotherapy outcomes. The review does not explicitly describe a meta-analysis or consensus process, but it summarizes key results from these trials.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that adjuvant radiotherapy for early oral cavity cancer with intermediate-risk features can reduce locoregional recurrence. Additionally, it notes that the DFS benefit of nivolumab in combined radioimmunotherapy (RIT) is maintained in patients with extensive neck dissection, suggesting that regional lymph nodes may not be as critical for immune response as previously thought. However, the results for RIT in HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer are conflicting, with the CCTG HN.9 trial failing to meet its efficacy endpoint and the KEYCHAIN trial showing significant improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) compared with cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is controversy regarding the efficacy of combined radioimmunotherapy (RIT) in HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer, as the CCTG HN.9 trial did not meet its efficacy endpoint while the KEYCHAIN trial showed significant improvement in PFS. Additionally, the review notes that subgroup analyses of the KEYNOTE-412 trial emphasize the importance of biomarker-based patient selection when combining radiotherapy and immunotherapy, indicating a gap in understanding how to optimally select patients for such treatments.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on refining biomarker-based patient selection for combined radiotherapy and immunotherapy approaches in HPV-associated cancers. It also highlights the need for further studies to resolve the conflicting results on the efficacy of RIT in HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer. In practice, these findings may inform treatment strategies for patients with HPV-associated head and neck cancers, particularly those with intermediate-risk features or extensive neck dissection.

analysis.summary_en: This review summarizes key findings from the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting on the role of human papillomaviruses (HPV) in head and neck cancer, particularly in relation to radiotherapy. It highlights that adjuvant radiotherapy can reduce locoregional recurrence in early oral cavity cancer with intermediate-risk features. However, results for combined radioimmunotherapy (RIT) in HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer are conflicting, with some trials showing no benefit and others demonstrating improved progression-free survival. The review also emphasizes the importance of biomarker-based patient selection in these treatment approaches. These findings suggest the need for further research to clarify the efficacy of RIT and to optimize patient selection for combined therapies.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 在头颈癌中的作用,特别是与放射治疗及其对局部复发和生存结果的影响有关。核心问题是口咽癌等 HPV 相关疾病是否受益于特定的放射治疗方法,包括联合放射免疫治疗。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查基于 2026 年 ASCO 年会的结果,包括 III 期 AREST 试验、JCOG1008 试验的事后分析以及 NIVOPOSTOP 和 KEYNOTE-412 试验的亚组分析。这些研究的选择是基于它们与 HPV 相关疾病的相关性以及它们对放射治疗结果的关注。该综述没有明确描述荟萃分析或共识过程,但总结了这些试验的主要结果。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述强调,对具有中等风险特征的早期口腔癌进行辅助放疗可以减少局部复发。此外,它指出,纳武单抗在联合放射​​免疫治疗 (RIT) 中的 DFS 益处在广泛颈清扫患者中得以维持,这表明区域淋巴结对于 免疫应答 可能并不像之前认为的那么重要。然而,RIT 在 HPV 阳性口咽癌中的结果是相互矛盾的,CCTG HN.9 试验未能达到其疗效终点,而 KEYCHAIN 试验显示与基于顺铂的放化疗相比,无进展生存期 (PFS) 显着改善。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 关于联合放射免疫治疗 (RIT) 对 HPV 阳性口咽癌的疗效存在争议,因为 CCTG HN.9 试验未达到其疗效终点,而 KEYCHAIN 试验显示 PFS 显着改善。此外,该评论指出,KEYNOTE-412 试验的亚组分析强调了在放射治疗和免疫治疗相结合时基于生物标志物的患者选择的重要性,这表明在理解如何为此类 治疗 最佳选择患者方面存在差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述表明,未来的研究应重点关注针对 HPV 相关癌症的联合放疗和免疫治疗方法,完善基于生物标志物的患者选择。它还强调需要进一步研究来解决 RIT 对 HPV 阳性口咽癌疗效的相互矛盾的结果。在实践中,这些发现可能为 HPV 相关头颈癌患者的 治疗 策略提供参考,特别是那些具有中等风险特征或广泛颈清扫术的患者。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the role of human papillomaviruses (HPV) in the context of head and neck cancer, particularly in relation to radiotherapy and its impact on locoregional recurrence and survival outcomes. The central question is whether HPV-associated diseases, such as oropharyngeal cancer, benefit from specific radiotherapy approaches, including combined radioimmunotherapy.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on findings from the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting, including the phase III AREST trial, the post hoc analysis of the JCOG1008 trial, and subgroup analyses from the NIVOPOSTOP and KEYNOTE-412 trials. These studies were selected based on their relevance to HPV-associated diseases and their focus on radiotherapy outcomes. The review does not explicitly describe a meta-analysis or consensus process, but it summarizes key results from these trials.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that adjuvant radiotherapy for early oral cavity cancer with intermediate-risk features can reduce locoregional recurrence. Additionally, it notes that the DFS benefit of nivolumab in combined radioimmunotherapy (RIT) is maintained in patients with extensive neck dissection, suggesting that regional lymph nodes may not be as critical for immune response as previously thought. However, the results for RIT in HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer are conflicting, with the CCTG HN.9 trial failing to meet its efficacy endpoint and the KEYCHAIN trial showing significant improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) compared with cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is controversy regarding the efficacy of combined radioimmunotherapy (RIT) in HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer, as the CCTG HN.9 trial did not meet its efficacy endpoint while the KEYCHAIN trial showed significant improvement in PFS. Additionally, the review notes that subgroup analyses of the KEYNOTE-412 trial emphasize the importance of biomarker-based patient selection when combining radiotherapy and immunotherapy, indicating a gap in understanding how to optimally select patients for such treatments.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on refining biomarker-based patient selection for combined radiotherapy and immunotherapy approaches in HPV-associated cancers. It also highlights the need for further studies to resolve the conflicting results on the efficacy of RIT in HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer. In practice, these findings may inform treatment strategies for patients with HPV-associated head and neck cancers, particularly those with intermediate-risk features or extensive neck dissection.

title_zh: [头颈癌的放射治疗:2026 年 ASCO 年会亮点]。
source_body_en: At the 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting, several studies focused on radiotherapy of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). The phase III AREST trial showed that adjuvant radiotherapy for early oral cavity cancer with intermediate-risk features can reduce the risk of locoregional recurrence. A post hoc analysis of the JCOG1008 trial found no increased locoregional recurrence rate even when adjuvant chemoradiotherapy was initiated later than recommended. Combined radioimmunotherapy (RIT) was also a major topic this year: in a subgroup analysis of the NIVOPOSTOP trial, the disease-free survival (DFS) benefit of nivolumab was maintained in patients with extensive neck dissection, which weakens the frequently highlighted mechanistic relevance of regional lymph nodes for the immune response. In the treatment of human papillomavirus (HPV)-positive oropharyngeal cancer, results for RIT were conflicting: the phase II CCTG HN.9 trial evaluating radiotherapy combined with durvalumab failed to meet its efficacy endpoint, whereas the phase II KEYCHAIN trial of definitive RIT with pembrolizumab demonstrated a significant improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) compared with cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy. In addition, a subgroup analysis of the combined positive score (CPS) ≥ 10 population of the KEYNOTE-412 trial underscored the importance of biomarker-based patient selection when combining radiotherapy and immunotherapy.
abstract_zh: 在2026年美国临床肿瘤学会(ASCO)年会上,多项研究聚焦于头颈鳞状细胞癌(HNSCC)的放射治疗。III期AREST试验表明,对具有中危特征的早期口腔癌进行辅助放疗可以降低局部复发的风险。JCOG1008 试验的事后分析发现,即使辅助放化疗开始时间晚于推荐时间,局部复发率也没有增加。联合放射免疫治疗 (RIT) 也是今年的一个主要话题:在 NIVOPOSTOP 试验的亚组分析中,纳武单抗在广泛颈清扫患者中维持了无病生存 (DFS) 益处,这削弱了经常强调的区域淋巴结与 免疫应答 的机械相关性。在 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 阳性口咽癌的 治疗 中,RIT 的结果是相互矛盾的:评估放疗联合 durvalumab 的 II 期 CCTG HN.9 试验未能达到其疗效终点,而联合派姆单抗确定性 RIT 的 II 期 KEYCHAIN 试验表明,与基于顺铂的放化疗相比,无进展生存期 (PFS) 显着改善。此外,对 KEYNOTE-412 试验的综合阳性评分 (CPS) ≥ 10 人群进行的亚组分析强调了结合放疗和免疫治疗时基于生物标志物的患者选择的重要性。

title: Awareness and knowledge of cervical cancer prevention and HPV vaccination among university students in Pakistan: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract Background Cervical cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths among women worldwide, despite being largely preventable. Its burden remains high in settings without organized vaccination and screening programs. Knowledge and awareness of cervical cancer prevention and human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination may influence the acceptance of preventive measures. This study aimed to assess knowledge and awareness of cervical cancer prevention and HPV vaccination among university students in Lahore, Pakistan, and to identify their main sources of health information. Methods A structured, quantitative, online survey in English was administered to students enrolled in medical-related programs at the University of Lahore, Pakistan. Results A total of 163 students participated. Knowledge of cervical cancer, HPV, and preventive measures was low to moderate. Only 69 participants (42%) recognized HPV infection as a risk factor, and 56 (34%) were unaware that cervical cancer can be prevented through Pap smear screening. Among female respondents, only 10 (12%) perceived themselves to be at risk. Knowledge of HPV transmission and vaccination was limited, with uncertainty regarding the purpose, timing, and benefits. Willingness to receive the HPV vaccine was moderate (62%). The main sources of health information were educational institutions, social media, and healthcare professionals, with healthcare professionals and educational institutions reported as the most trusted. Conclusions Despite a relatively educated population, knowledge of cervical cancer prevention and HPV vaccination remains insufficient. Targeted educational interventions and comprehensive public health strategies, including culturally sensitive communication and access to vaccination and screening programs, are essential to enhance preventive outcomes.

title_zh: 巴基斯坦大学生对 宫颈癌 预防和 HPV 疫苗接种 的认识和了解:一项横断面研究
source_body_en: Abstract Background Cervical cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths among women worldwide, despite being largely preventable. Its burden remains high in settings without organized vaccination and screening programs. Knowledge and awareness of cervical cancer prevention and human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination may influence the acceptance of preventive measures. This study aimed to assess knowledge and awareness of cervical cancer prevention and HPV vaccination among university students in Lahore, Pakistan, and to identify their main sources of health information. Methods A structured, quantitative, online survey in English was administered to students enrolled in medical-related programs at the University of Lahore, Pakistan. Results A total of 163 students participated. Knowledge of cervical cancer, HPV, and preventive measures was low to moderate. Only 69 participants (42%) recognized HPV infection as a risk factor, and 56 (34%) were unaware that cervical cancer can be prevented through Pap smear screening. Among female respondents, only 10 (12%) perceived themselves to be at risk. Knowledge of HPV transmission and vaccination was limited, with uncertainty regarding the purpose, timing, and benefits. Willingness to receive the HPV vaccine was moderate (62%). The main sources of health information were educational institutions, social media, and healthcare professionals, with healthcare professionals and educational institutions reported as the most trusted. Conclusions Despite a relatively educated population, knowledge of cervical cancer prevention and HPV vaccination remains insufficient. Targeted educational interventions and comprehensive public health strategies, including culturally sensitive communication and access to vaccination and screening programs, are essential to enhance preventive outcomes.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 宫颈癌 是全球女性癌症相关死亡的主要原因之一,尽管在很大程度上是可以预防的。在没有有组织的 疫苗接种 和筛查计划的情况下,其负担仍然很高。对 宫颈癌 预防和 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗接种 的了解和认识可能会影响对预防措施的接受。本研究旨在评估巴基斯坦拉合尔大学生对 宫颈癌 预防和 HPV 疫苗接种 的了解和认识,并确定他们健康信息的主要来源。方法 对巴基斯坦拉合尔大学医学相关课程的学生进行了结构化、定量的在线英语调查。结果共有163名学生参加。对 宫颈癌、HPV 和预防措施的了解程度为低至中等。只有 69 名参与者 (42%) 认为 HPV 感染是一个危险因素,56 名参与者 (34%) 不知道可以通过巴氏涂片筛查来预防 宫颈癌。在女性受访者中,只有 10 人(12%)认为自己面临风险。对 HPV 传播 和 疫苗接种 的了解有限,其目的、时机和益处尚不确定。接受 HPV 疫苗 的意愿中等 (62%)。健康信息的主要来源是教育机构、社交媒体和医疗保健专业人员,其中医疗保健专业人员和教育机构被认为是最值得信赖的。结论 尽管人群受教育程度相对较高,但对 宫颈癌 预防和 HPV 疫苗接种 的了解仍然不足。有针对性的教育干预措施和全面的公共卫生策略,包括文化敏感的沟通以及获得 疫苗接种 和筛查计划,对于增强预防效果至关重要。

title: A qualitative evaluation of a STEAM (Science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics) peer education intervention on teenagers' knowledge, confidence, and advocacy for HPV vaccine communication.
abstract: Vaccine hesitancy is a rising global phenomenon. Ireland experienced a crisis in confidence and vaccine decline for the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine in 2015, with rapid national efforts to address concerns and improve uptake rates. We developed a unique STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics) peer education intervention through an interdisciplinary team (immunologist, educationalist, designer, filmmaker, and psychologist) to address vaccine hesitancy and utilize peer education, which is promising but underused in the literature. We aimed to evaluate the effect of our STEAM intervention on Irish teenagers' knowledge and confidence in advocacy for the HPV vaccine to their younger peers facing their HPV vaccine offer. We used qualitative methods consisting of 12 focus group discussions with teens (n = 53), one qualitative in-class evaluation among younger peers (n = 35), and knowledge exit slips (n = 300) to evaluate teenagers' knowledge, confidence, advocacy, and younger peers' knowledge. Data were analyzed inductively using reflexive thematic analysis. Our overall egalitarian theme indicated democratic participation by teenagers with three related themes that were compatible with behavior as a vaccine advocate. Teenagers reported positive changes overall in HPV knowledge, confidence, and advocacy beliefs following the intervention. Younger peers could recall HPV facts and knowledge during in-class evaluations and exit slips. We conclude that scaffolding through our STEAM intervention enabled Irish teenagers to feel empowered to act as vaccine advocates. Peer education within our intervention shows promise in raising HPV awareness and knowledge and could be explored in wider contexts.

title: Phenolic Hydroxyl-Containing Lipid Nanoparticles Enable Codelivery of HPV Peptide Antigens and Manganese Adjuvant for Cancer Immunotherapy.
abstract: Abstract Therapeutic peptide vaccines against HPV-associated cancers are often limited by insufficient immunogenicity and inefficient intracellular delivery. Here, we develop a phenolic hydroxyl-containing lipid nanoparticle (EMT@LNP) as a nanomedicine platform for the coordinated codelivery of HPV16 E6/E7 peptide antigens and manganese (Mn2+) adjuvant. Distinct from conventional electrostatic loading strategies, EMT@LNP exploits hydrogen-bonding interactions between phenolic hydroxyl groups and peptide antigens, enabling charge-independent loading of peptides with diverse physicochemical properties, while coordination interactions between phenolic moieties and Mn2+ allow the simultaneous incorporation of immunostimulatory adjuvants. This dual-interaction-driven design integrates antigen delivery and innate immune activation within a single nanostructure. Functionally, EMT@LNP enhances antigen uptake and promotes dendritic cell maturation, accompanied by activation of STING-associated signaling, as indicated by increased phosphorylation of STING, TBK1, and IRF3. In vivo, EMT@LNP facilitates efficient delivery to draining lymph nodes and prolongs antigen retention following intramuscular administration. In a therapeutic TC-1 tumor model, EMT@LNP elicits potent antitumor immune responses, characterized by enhanced CD8+ T-cell infiltration and reduced immunosuppressive cell populations, leading to significant tumor growth inhibition without observable systemic toxicity. Collectively, this study presents a nanobiotechnology strategy that combines charge-independent peptide loading with metal-ion-mediated immune activation, providing a versatile and potentially translatable platform for therapeutic vaccination against HPV-associated malignancies.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a novel nanomedicine platform, EMT@LNP, designed to enhance therapeutic peptide vaccines against HPV-associated cancers. The platform leverages hydrogen-bonding interactions for charge-independent peptide loading and coordination interactions for incorporating manganese adjuvants. It demonstrates improved antigen uptake, dendritic cell maturation, and STING signaling activation in vitro, along with efficient lymph node delivery and prolonged antigen retention in vivo. In a TC-1 tumor model, EMT@LNP elicited strong antitumor immune responses, including enhanced CD8+ T-cell infiltration and reduced immunosuppressive cell populations, resulting in significant tumor growth inhibition without systemic toxicity. The study presents a promising strategy for therapeutic vaccination against HPV-related malignancies, though the evidence is based on abstract-only data and in vivo models, limiting its clinical applicability. The findings suggest potential for improved immunotherapeutic approaches but require further validation in clinical settings.

abstract_zh: 摘要 针对 HPV 相关癌症的治疗性肽 疫苗 通常受到免疫原性不足和细胞内递送效率低下的限制。在这里,我们开发了一种含酚羟基的脂质纳米颗粒(EMT@LNP)作为纳米医学平台,用于协调共递送 HPV16 E6/E7 肽抗原和锰(Mn2+)佐剂。与传统的静电负载策略不同,EMT@LNP利用酚羟基和肽抗原之间的氢键相互作用,实现具有不同理化性质的肽的电荷独立负载,而酚部分和Mn2+之间的配位相互作用允许同时掺入免疫刺激佐剂。这种双重相互作用驱动的设计将抗原递送和先天免疫激活集成在单个纳米结构内。从功能上讲,EMT@LNP 增强抗原摄取并促进树突状细胞成熟,同时激活 STING 相关信号传导,如 STING、TBK1 和 IRF3 磷酸化增加所示。在体内,EMT@LNP 有助于有效递送至引流淋巴结,并延长肌肉注射后的抗原保留时间。在治疗性 TC-1 肿瘤模型中,EMT@LNP 引发有效的抗肿瘤 免疫应答,其特点是增强 CD8+ T 细胞浸润和减少免疫抑制细胞群,从而导致显着的肿瘤生长抑制,且没有可观察到的全身毒性。总的来说,这项研究提出了一种纳米生物技术策略,将电荷无关的肽负载与金属离子介导的免疫激活相结合,为 疫苗接种 治疗 HPV 相关恶性肿瘤提供了一个多功能且潜在可转化的平台。

analysis_zh.main_results: 从功能上讲,EMT@LNP 增强了抗原摄取并促进树突状细胞成熟,同时激活 STING 相关信号传导,如 STING、TBK1 和 IRF3 磷酸化增加所示。在体内,它有助于有效递送至引流淋巴结并延长肌肉注射后的抗原保留时间。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为一种新颖的纳米生物技术策略的证据,该策略将电荷无关的肽负载与金属离子介导的免疫激活相结合,为 疫苗接种 治疗 HPV 相关恶性肿瘤提供了一个多功能平台。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,EMT@LNP 可以为针对 HPV 相关癌症开发更有效的治疗药物 疫苗 提供信息,从而有可能改善免疫原性和 治疗 结局。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于抽象分析,证据基于体外和体内模型,可能无法完全代表临床情况。证据强度中等。

title: Vaccines for Cancer: A Translational Science Review.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Advances in tumor immunology and vaccine technology are reshaping cancer vaccine development after decades of limited clinical success. More than 2000 immunogenic tumor proteins or antigens have been identified, the types of immune responses required for tumor eradication have been defined, and safe and effective vaccine delivery technologies have been developed. This progress has renewed clinical investigation of cancer vaccines for multiple types of cancer. OBSERVATIONS: Vaccines, such as those against human papillomavirus and hepatitis B, are composed of (1) an antigen target, (2) an adjuvant to activate the immune system, and (3) a vaccine delivery vehicle. Antigens can be derived from tumor mutations termed neoantigens, or cancer-associated nonmutated proteins, which are normal human proteins that are abnormally expressed in cancer. The tumor can also act as an antigen source, such as when immunization occurs with whole tumor cells or by directly injecting an immunogenic substance into the tumor to elicit an adaptive immune response. T and B lymphocytes, cells of the adaptive immune system, are stimulated by cancer vaccines and can provide a highly specific and durable immune response directed against cancer. Vaccines that elicit adaptive immunity are approved for cancer treatment. Sipuleucel-T, a vaccine against the antigen prostatic acid phosphatase, reduced all-cause mortality compared with placebo in men with metastatic castrate-resistant prostate cancer (32% vs 23%; hazard ratio, 0.78 [95% CI, 0.61-0.98]; P = .03). Compared with granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor, a systemic immune stimulant, talimogene laherparepvec increased rates of a 6-month or longer complete or partial response, defined as the disappearance of all treated disease and at least a 50% decrease in the sum of the products of perpendicular diameters of the measurable lesion with no new lesions, respectively, when injected into advanced melanoma lesions (16.3% [95% CI, 12.1%-20.5%] vs 2.1% [95% CI, 0%-4.5%]; odds ratio, 8.9; P < .001). Most cancer vaccines have mild adverse effects, such as fatigue, fever, and injection site reactions. Combining cancer vaccines with chemotherapy or immunotherapy can increase the magnitude of the immune response and potentially result in greater reduction in cancer size. Combining the personalized mutation-based messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccine (mRNA-4157) with the immune checkpoint inhibitor pembrolizumab for resected high-risk stage IIIB to IV cutaneous melanoma improved relapse-free survival compared with pembrolizumab alone (76.6% vs 60%; hazard ratio, 0.56 [95% CI, 0.31-1.02]; P = .05). Cancer vaccines are undergoing evaluation in clinical trials to prevent cancer recurrence and for primary cancer prevention. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Cancer vaccines can treat several types of malignant neoplasms, including melanoma, prostate cancer, and bladder cancer. Adverse effects associated with cancer vaccines are generally mild and of short duration, promoting eventual integration of vaccination into treatment regimens with chemotherapy and immunotherapy. Cancer vaccines are increasingly undergoing evaluation for primary prevention.

title_original: Vaccines for Cancer: A Translational Science Review.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on cancer vaccines, particularly those targeting human papillomaviruses (HPV), with an emphasis on their role in treating and preventing HPV-associated malignancies such as cervical, anal, and oropharyngeal cancers. The central question is whether cancer vaccines can effectively treat and prevent these specific HPV-related diseases.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of cancer vaccines, including their development, mechanisms, and clinical applications. It references studies on vaccines like Sipuleucel-T and talimogene laherparepvec, which are evaluated for their efficacy in treating specific cancers. The review also discusses the general progress in identifying immunogenic tumor proteins and developing safe vaccine delivery technologies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Cancer vaccines have shown efficacy in treating certain HPV-associated cancers, such as melanoma, prostate cancer, and bladder cancer. These vaccines stimulate T and B lymphocytes to produce a specific and durable immune response against cancer. Additionally, they are being evaluated for primary prevention of cancer recurrence and for preventing cancer in the first place.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights that while some vaccines have demonstrated effectiveness, the evidence for their use in other cancers remains limited. There are also gaps in understanding the long-term effects of these vaccines and their potential for broader application across different cancer types.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to evaluate the effectiveness of cancer vaccines in preventing cancer recurrence and for primary prevention. Clinical trials should focus on expanding the use of these vaccines to other HPV-associated cancers and improving their integration with existing treatments like chemotherapy and immunotherapy.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the development and application of cancer vaccines targeting human papillomaviruses (HPV), emphasizing their role in treating and preventing HPV-associated malignancies such as cervical, anal, and oropharyngeal cancers. It highlights the progress in identifying immunogenic tumor proteins and safe vaccine delivery technologies, as well as the clinical success of vaccines like Sipuleucel-T and talimogene laherparepvec. The review concludes that these vaccines can treat several cancers, including melanoma, prostate cancer, and bladder cancer, and are being evaluated for primary prevention. However, there are controversies and evidence gaps regarding their broader application and long-term effects. Research and clinical trials are recommended to further assess their potential in preventing cancer recurrence and for primary prevention.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述的重点是癌症 疫苗,特别是那些针对 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 的药物,重点是它们在治疗和预防 HPV 相关恶性肿瘤(如宫颈癌、肛门癌和口咽癌)中的作用。核心问题是癌症疫苗能否有效治疗和预防这些特定的HPV相关疾病。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对癌症 疫苗 的系统分析,包括其发展、机制和临床应用。它引用了 疫苗 的研究,例如 Sipuleucel-T 和 talimogene laherparepvec,这些研究评估了它们在治疗特定癌症方面的功效。该综述还讨论了识别免疫原性肿瘤蛋白和开发安全的 疫苗 递送技术的总体进展。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 癌症 疫苗 已显示出治疗某些 HPV 相关癌症的功效,例如黑色素瘤、前列腺癌和膀胱癌。这些 疫苗 刺激 T 和 B 淋巴细胞产生特异性且持久的 免疫应答 抗癌药物。此外,正在对它们进行癌症复发一级预防和预防癌症的评估。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该评论强调,虽然一些 疫苗 已被证明有效,但其用于其他癌症的证据仍然有限。在理解这些 疫苗 的长期影响及其在不同癌症类型中更广泛应用的潜力方面也存在差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要进一步的研究来评估癌症 疫苗 在预防癌症复发和一级预防方面的有效性。临床试验应侧重于将这些 疫苗 的使用范围扩大到其他 HPV 相关癌症,并改善其与现有 治疗(如化疗和免疫疗法)的整合。

title: Navigating HPV vaccination challenges in low-resource settings: Practical strategies for estimating the size of out-of-school girls.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Achieving the 2030 target of 90% human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination coverage among girls by age 15 requires effectively reaching out-of-school (OOS) girls, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) where most vaccine delivery occurs in school settings. This study explored country definitions of OOS girls and strategies for estimating the size of this population. METHODS: Between May and September 2024, we conducted semi-structured in-depth interviews with 32 HPV vaccine program stakeholders across six African and Asian LMICs with established HPV vaccination programs: Cambodia, Cameroon, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, and Uganda. Using hybrid inductive-deductive thematic analyses, we identified country approaches to defining OOS girls and to enumerating or estimating population size. RESULTS: Administratively, countries commonly defined OOS girls as those not enrolled in schools under the Ministry of Education's purview, but in practice, definitions varied across contexts. National-level data (e.g., census, school enrollment rates) and household-level approaches (e.g., headcounts) were commonly used to enumerate in-school and OOS girls. However, the distinction between in-school and OOS girls was often blurred during HPV vaccination implementation and evaluation, limiting the operational utility of these methods. To address these challenges, some countries adopted alternative approaches, including proxy-based population estimates using historical or approximate data and the prioritization of areas perceived to have a higher presence of OOS girls. These alternative approaches were perceived as pragmatic compromises between accuracy, feasibility, and resource constraints. CONCLUSION: Accurate enumeration of OOS girls is important for HPV vaccination but may not be feasible in resource-limited settings. Pragmatic, context-specific estimation methods can offer a feasible way to identify and reach OOS girls more effectively with HPV vaccination services.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在探讨各国对失学 (OOS) 女童的定义以及估算中低收入国家 (LMIC) 女童人口规模的策略,以应对在 2030 年实现 15 岁女童 HPV 疫苗接种 覆盖率 90% 的目标方面所面临的挑战。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究于 2024 年 5 月至 9 月期间对来自 6 个非洲和亚洲中低收入国家(柬埔寨、喀麦隆、肯尼亚、马拉维、莫桑比克和乌干达)的 32 名 HPV 疫苗 项目利益相关者进行了半结构化深入访谈。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用半结构化深入访谈和混合归纳演绎主题分析来确定各国定义 OOS 女孩并估计其人口规模的方法。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究发现,各国通常在行政上将失学女童定义为未在教育部管辖范围内的学校就读的女童,但实践中的定义各不相同。使用国家层面的数据和家庭层面的方法来统计在校女童和失学女童,但在 HPV 疫苗接种 实施和评估过程中,在校女童和失学女童之间的区别常常变得模糊。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究强调需要采用务实、针对具体情况的估计方法,以通过 HPV 疫苗接种 服务准确识别和更有效地接触 OOS 女孩。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore country definitions of out-of-school (OOS) girls and strategies for estimating their population size in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) to address challenges in achieving the 2030 target of 90% HPV vaccination coverage among girls by age 15.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study involved semi-structured in-depth interviews with 32 HPV vaccine program stakeholders from six African and Asian LMICs: Cambodia, Cameroon, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, and Uganda, conducted between May and September 2024.
analysis_en.methods: The researchers used semi-structured in-depth interviews and hybrid inductive-deductive thematic analyses to identify country approaches to defining OOS girls and estimating their population size.
analysis_en.main_results: The study found that countries commonly defined OOS girls administratively as those not enrolled in schools under the Ministry of Education's purview, but definitions varied in practice. National-level data and household-level approaches were used to enumerate in-school and OOS girls, but the distinction between in-school and OOS girls was often blurred during HPV vaccination implementation and evaluation.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlighted the need for pragmatic, context-specific estimation methods to accurately identify and reach OOS girls more effectively with HPV vaccination services.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform strategies for improving the operational utility of methods to enumerate OOS girls and enhance the reach of HPV vaccination programs in resource-limited settings.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's reliance on interviews and thematic analyses limits the generalizability of the findings. The distinction between in-school and OOS girls was often blurred, which may affect the accuracy of population estimates.

title_zh: 在资源匮乏的环境中应对 HPV 疫苗接种 挑战:估计失学女孩体型的实用策略。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Achieving the 2030 target of 90% human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination coverage among girls by age 15 requires effectively reaching out-of-school (OOS) girls, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) where most vaccine delivery occurs in school settings. This study explored country definitions of OOS girls and strategies for estimating the size of this population. METHODS: Between May and September 2024, we conducted semi-structured in-depth interviews with 32 HPV vaccine program stakeholders across six African and Asian LMICs with established HPV vaccination programs: Cambodia, Cameroon, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, and Uganda. Using hybrid inductive-deductive thematic analyses, we identified country approaches to defining OOS girls and to enumerating or estimating population size. RESULTS: Administratively, countries commonly defined OOS girls as those not enrolled in schools under the Ministry of Education's purview, but in practice, definitions varied across contexts. National-level data (e.g., census, school enrollment rates) and household-level approaches (e.g., headcounts) were commonly used to enumerate in-school and OOS girls. However, the distinction between in-school and OOS girls was often blurred during HPV vaccination implementation and evaluation, limiting the operational utility of these methods. To address these challenges, some countries adopted alternative approaches, including proxy-based population estimates using historical or approximate data and the prioritization of areas perceived to have a higher presence of OOS girls. These alternative approaches were perceived as pragmatic compromises between accuracy, feasibility, and resource constraints. CONCLUSION: Accurate enumeration of OOS girls is important for HPV vaccination but may not be feasible in resource-limited settings. Pragmatic, context-specific estimation methods can offer a feasible way to identify and reach OOS girls more effectively with HPV vaccination services.
abstract_zh: 背景:要实现 2030 年 15 岁女孩 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗接种 覆盖率达到 90% 的目标,需要有效覆盖失学 (OOS) 女孩,特别是在大多数 疫苗 分娩发生在学校环境中的低收入和中等收入国家 (LMIC)。本研究探讨了各国对 OOS 女孩的定义以及估计该人口规模的策略。方法:2024 年 5 月至 9 月期间,我们对 6 个已建立 HPV 疫苗接种 项目的非洲和亚洲中低收入国家的 32 名 HPV 疫苗 项目利益相关者进行了半结构化深度访谈:柬埔寨、喀麦隆、肯尼亚、马拉维、莫桑比克和乌干达。通过混合归纳演绎主题分析,我们确定了各国定义 OOS 女孩以及计算或估计人口规模的方法。结果:在行政上,各国通常将失学女童定义为未在教育部管辖范围内的学校就读的女童,但在实践中,不同背景下的定义有所不同。国家层面的数据(例如人口普查、入学率)和家庭层面的方法(例如人数)通常用于统计在校女童和离校女童。然而,在 HPV 疫苗接种 实施和评估过程中,在校女孩和 OOS 女孩之间的区别往往很模糊,限制了这些方法的操作效用。为了应对这些挑战,一些国家采取了替代方法,包括使用历史或近似数据进行基于代理的人口估计,以及优先考虑被认为存在离校女童较多的地区。这些替代方法被认为是准确性、可行性和资源限制之间的务实妥协。结论:准确计数 OOS 女孩对于 HPV 疫苗接种 很重要,但在资源有限的环境中可能不可行。务实、针对具体情况的估计方法可以提供一种可行的方法,通过 HPV 疫苗接种 服务更有效地识别和接触 OOS 女孩。

title: Assessment of natural killer cell activity in HPV-infected women - a cross-sectional study.
abstract: Objectives: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infections, particularly high-risk oncogenic types, are linked to cervical and other anogenital cancers. Natural killer (NK) cells play a vital role in the innate immune response, identifying and eliminating virus-infected cells without prior sensitization. Material and methods: This study compares serum NK cell activity in women with oncogenic HPV infections and HPV-negative controls. Understanding differences in NK cell activity may provide insights into HPV clearance mechanisms and potential immunotherapeutic targets. Methods: A prospective cohort study was conducted at Gaziantep University Hospital, enrolling patients over 12 months. Participants were categorized based on HPV status, and blood samples were analyzed to quantitatively assess serum NK cell activity using an ELISA-based assay. Results: Among 82 women, 20 tested positive for HPV 16/18, 35 had other high-risk oncogenic HPV types, and 27 were HPV negative. NK cell activity did not significantly differ between HPV 16/18 and other high-risk HPV groups (p = 0.544). However, the HPV-negative group had significantly higher NK cell activity than both HPV-positive groups (p = 0.001 and p = 0.002). Conclusions: Reduced NK cell activity may contribute to persistent oncogenic HPV infections. These findings suggest a potential role for NK cell-modulating therapies to enhance HPV clearance.

abstract_zh: 目的:人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染,尤其是高风险致癌类型,与宫颈癌和其他肛门生殖器癌有关。自然杀伤 (NK) 细胞在先天 免疫应答 中发挥着至关重要的作用,无需事先致敏即可识别并消除病毒感染的细胞。材料和方法:本研究比较了致癌 HPV 感染女性和 HPV 阴性对照女性的血清 NK 细胞活性。了解 NK 细胞活性的差异可能有助于深入了解 HPV 清除机制和潜在的免疫治疗靶点。方法:在加济安泰普大学医院进行了一项前瞻性 队列研究 研究,招募了超过 12 个月的患者。根据 HPV 状态对参与者进行分类,并使用基于 ELISA 的检测分析血液样本以定量评估血清 NK 细胞活性。结果:在 82 名女性中,20 名 HPV 16/18 检测呈阳性,35 名患有其他高危致癌 HPV 类型,27 名 HPV 阴性。HPV 16/18 和其他 高危型HPV 组之间的 NK 细胞活性没有显着差异 (p = 0.544)。然而,HPV 阴性组的 NK 细胞活性显着高于 HPV 阳性组(p = 0.001 和 p = 0.002)。结论:NK 细胞活性降低可能导致持续致癌 HPV 感染。这些发现表明 NK 细胞调节疗法在增强 HPV 清除方面具有潜在作用。

title: E2 displacement of CIP2A from TOPBP1 activates the DNA damage response during papillomavirus life cycles.
abstract: The papillomavirus life cycle is linked to epithelial differentiation, and the virus manipulates differentiation to facilitate viral production. One such manipulation is the activation of the DNA damage response (DDR), which promotes viral replication via homologous recombination. Here, we show that the papillomavirus transcription/replication/segregation factor E2 activates the DDR. During differentiation, E2 attenuates sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) activity, enhances the acetylation of DDR factors, and displaces cancerous inhibitor of protein phosphatase 2A (CIP2A) from DNA topoisomerase II-binding protein 1 (TOPBP1), resulting in CIP2A-mediated inhibition of protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) and ataxia-telangiectasia mutated (ATM) activation. E2 associates with TOPBP1 and ATM while reducing TOPBP1-ATR complexes and ataxia-telangiectasia and Rad3-related (ATR) activation. This ATM-high, ATR-low DDR phenotype promotes viral replication and cell proliferation. We observe this DDR activation in E2-expressing keratinocytes, human papillomavirus 16 (HPV16)-positive cells, Mus musculus papillomavirus 1 (MmuPV1)-induced lesions, HPV-positive head and neck cancer cell lines, and HPV16-positive patient-derived xenografts. ATM inhibition preferentially kills E2-expressing cells, supporting ATM signaling as a potential therapeutic target in HPV-associated disease retaining E2 expression and episomal genomes.

title: Patient Experiences With ctHPVDNA-Guided Surveillance for HPV-Positive Oropharyngeal Cancer.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Circulating tumor human papillomavirus DNA (ctHPVDNA) is a potential biomarker for surveillance of HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer. Despite its growing clinical use, patient experiences are not well characterized, and understanding patient perspectives of ctHPVDNA-guided surveillance is essential to guiding its appropriate use while mitigating potential harms. OBJECTIVE: To characterize patient experiences with ctHPVDNA-guided surveillance. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: A mixed-methods cross-sectional interview study in adults treated for HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer with 1 or more surveillance ctHPVDNA test 3 or more months before enrollment conducted in June through August 2025 in a single tertiary academic cancer center. Purposive sampling ensured representation of diverse patient experiences. EXPOSURES: One semistructured interview regarding experiences with ctHPVDNA-guided surveillance. Willingness to pay (WTP) out of pocket was assessed using iterative bidding. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Themes and subthemes were derived from coded interview transcripts using a categorical inductive approach. RESULTS: Among 20 participants (median age, 58 years [IQR, 55-70 years]; 16 males [80%]), 8 (40%) had true-negative ctHPVDNA test results, 6 had true-positive results (30%), 4 had false-negative results (20%), and 2 had false-positive results (10%). Five major themes emerged: (1) broad enthusiasm and support for ctHPVDNA testing, with a common assumption that more and earlier disease-related information is beneficial, and appreciation for the reassurance of negative test results (discordance between support for testing in general and personal experiences of test accuracy was observed); (2) distress as inherent to the emotional variability of the cancer journey itself, such that anxiety associated with ctHPVDNA testing was considered attributable to cancer survivorship rather than to the test; (3) trust in the oncology team supersedes trust in test itself, whereby clinicians were trusted to appropriately interpret potentially confusing results (this trust was enhanced by clear communication); (4) test as a valuable add-on to standard care, which should enrich, but not replace, standard surveillance; and (5) sensitivity to financial toxicity, with strong support for accessible and equitable testing. The median per-test WTP was $325 (range, $0-$9000). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This study found that participants expressed strong support for ctHPVDNA-guided surveillance. Trust in clinicians appeared to mitigate distress related to confusing or inaccurate test results. Clinicians using ctHPVDNA testing should be familiar with and clearly communicate its strengths and limitations to optimize clinical benefit.

title: Mobile cervical screening: using an opportunistic screening service to increase uptake in underserved communities.
abstract: Attendance rates for the cervical screening programme and the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination programme in England have fallen since 2022. Women and all people with a cervix from underserved communities are known to have lower screening attendance rates than other groups, so it is vital to address barriers to attendance to increase screening uptake. This article describes a service innovation pilot project in north west England involving the delivery of opportunistic cervical screening via a mobile screening unit sited in convenient community locations. The aim was to identify precancerous changes and promote early treatment for moderate-to-severe dyskaryosis by increasing attendance rates among underserved communities. A total of 2,283 clients completed a cervical screen during the pilot period (between July 2024 and March 2026). Analysis showed that a significant percentage (44%, n =994) of clients were from the two lowest deciles of the Index of Multiple Deprivation; half ( n =1,145, 50%) of completed screens were for clients designated as 'non-responders' to screening invitations; 101 (4%) clients were referred for colposcopy; and 18 (1%) clients were identified as having high-grade dyskaryosis. Patient experience feedback suggests that the opportunistic nature of the service was a significant incentive for clients to attend for screening. The project is ongoing and the service aims to expand to cover the whole of NHS England North West.

title: Age-specific income losses due to HPV-attributable cancers in Singapore
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The link between Human Papillomavirus (HPV) and cancer is well-established. In Singapore, bivalent HPV vaccines are subsidised for females, but not males. Economic analysis of HPV vaccination has generally assessed the costs to the health system, but this may not be as relevant to individual decision-making as potential lost income. We estimated the impact of bivalent HPV 16/18 vaccination on sick leave, unemployment, and premature mortality as a function of age and sex to understand the broader impact of HPV-related cancers. METHODS: We developed a population-level economic model to estimate lifetime income losses by diagnosis age, sex and cancer type. We applied sex- and cancer-specific Cox regressions to the Singapore Cancer Registry for annual predicted survival from 1992 to 2022. These were combined with census and employment data to estimate HPV-associated income losses in Singapore. Attributable fractions and vaccine effectiveness data for HPV 16/18 from the literature were used to estimate the effectiveness of bivalent HPV vaccination. Structural sensitivity analysis examined the role of 80% population coverage conferring herd immunity. RESULTS: The registry contained 17,294 individuals with an HPV-associated cancer diagnosis. Lost income was greatest for cervical cancer due to its high prevalence, however the losses per diagnosis were highest for oropharyngeal cancer. Bivalent HPV vaccination led to income benefits of $SGD1,397 [$895 to $1,838] in girls and -$62 [-$76 to -$48] in boys. A gender-neutral HPV vaccination of 80% of 15-year-old Singaporeans, conferring herd immunity, would have lifetime income protective benefits of $24.4m [$14.2m, $33.7m] per cohort, a five-fold return on investment. CONCLUSIONS: In addition to avoiding healthcare costs and lost quality of life, parents should consider vaccination as a means of avoiding potential income losses. A national policy of gender-neutral HPV vaccination could deliver substantial income protection due to both individual vaccine protection and herd immunity.

title: Development of an HPV Self-Collection Brochure for Unhoused Individuals Using Learner Verification and Revision.
abstract: Individuals who are unhoused face disproportionately high rates of cervical cancer incidence and multiple barriers to screening, yet tailored educational materials to support human papillomavirus (HPV) self-collection in this population remain scarce. To address this gap, we conducted a sequential, two-phased qualitative study using Learner Verification and Revision methodology to iteratively develop and refine an instructional brochure on HPV self-collection designed for, and with, individuals who are unhoused. We first conducted focus groups with community health educators ( n = 6) and street medicine team members ( n = 12), followed by semi-structured interviews with individuals who were unhoused ( n = 19) and had participated in an HPV self-collection pilot study. Data collection assessed comprehension, attraction, cultural-linguistic acceptability, and persuasion of the brochure, with trauma-informed care as an additional domain, and transcripts were analyzed using thematic analysis. Participants broadly found the brochure clear, visually appealing, and easy to follow, while identifying key areas for refinement, including greater brevity, more inclusive visuals, regional Spanish vocabulary adaptation, and language modifications to strengthen trustworthiness and empowerment. Street medicine team members emphasized that the brochure best complements verbal counseling rather than serving as a standalone resource. This community-engaged, iterative process yielded a tailored, trauma-informed educational tool which is publicly available and editable. As HPV self-collection expands across the United States, such materials will be valuable to support equitable access to cervical cancer screening.

title: Cannabidiol impairs tumor-associated behaviors and modulates apoptosis- and autophagy-related pathways in cisplatin-resistant head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) remains a challenge due to recurrence, metastasis, and resistance to conventional therapies, particularly in human papillomavirus (HPV)-negative tumors. Cannabidiol (CBD), a non-psychoactive phytocannabinoid, has demonstrated antitumor activity in several cancer models; however, its effects in chemoresistant HNSCC are not well established. This study evaluates the antitumor effects of CBD and cellular mechanisms in a cisplatin -resistant, HPV-negative HNSCC model. Cytotoxic effects of CBD were assessed in HN13 cells and compared with fibroblasts and keratinocytes using MTT and selectivity index analysis. Migration, invasion, metalloproteinase activity, clonogenic survival, and cytotoxicity on 3D spheroids were evaluated. Cell death-related mechanisms were investigated using acridine orange/propidium iodide staining and Western blot analysis of apoptosis, autophagy, and cell-cycle regulation. Antitumor activity and vascular safety were further assessed using the chorioallantoic membrane model and HET-CAM assay. The combined effect of CBD and CIS was evaluated using the combination index analysis. CBD exhibited selective cytotoxicity toward HN13 cells and reduced migration, invasion, matrix metalloproteinase-2/9 activity, clonogenic survival, and 3D spheroid growth. CBD altered proteins associated with apoptosis, autophagy, and cell-cycle regulation. Pharmacological inhibition with 3-MA enhanced CBD-associated apoptotic signaling, increasing PARP and caspase-3 cleavage. In the CAM, CBD reduced tumor growth and vascular area without inducing vascular irritation. Furthermore, CBD and CIS demonstrated synergistic cytotoxic effects in HN13 cells. CBD exerted selective antitumor effects on CIS-resistant HN13 HNSCC cells, affecting tumor-associated behaviors and modulating apoptosis and autophagy-related signaling, while acting synergistically with cisplatin. These findings support further preclinical investigation of CBD as a potential adjunct approach in HNSCC, particularly in chemoresistant settings.
authors: Rosy Iara Maciel de Azambuja Ribeiro

Cannabidiol (CBD), a non-psychoactive phytocannabinoid, has demonstrated antitumor activity in several cancer models; however, its effects in chemoresistant HNSCC are not well established. This study evaluates the antitumor effects of CBD and cellular mechanisms in a cisplatin -resistant, HPV-negative HNSCC model. Cytotoxic effects of CBD were assessed in HN13 cells and compared with fibroblasts and keratinocytes using MTT and selectivity index analysis. Migration, invasion, metalloproteinase activity, clonogenic survival, and cytotoxicity on 3D spheroids were evaluated. Cell death-related mechanisms were investigated using acridine orange/propidium iodide staining and Western blot analysis of apoptosis, autophagy, and cell-cycle regulation. Antitumor activity and vascular safety were further assessed using the chorioallantoic membrane model and HET-CAM assay. The combined effect of CBD and CIS was evaluated using the combination index analysis. CBD exhibited selective cytotoxicity toward HN13 cells and reduced migration, invasion, matrix metalloproteinase-2/9 activity, clonogenic survival, and 3D spheroid growth. CBD altered proteins associated with apoptosis, autophagy, and cell-cycle regulation. Pharmacological inhibition with 3-MA enhanced CBD-associated apoptotic signaling, increasing PARP and caspase-3 cleavage. In the CAM, CBD reduced tumor growth and vascular area without inducing vascular irritation. Furthermore, CBD and CIS demonstrated synergistic cytotoxic effects in HN13 cells. CBD exerted selective antitumor effects on CIS-resistant HN13 HNSCC cells, affecting tumor-associated behaviors and modulating apoptosis and autophagy-related signaling, while acting synergistically with cisplatin. These findings support further preclinical investigation of CBD as a potential adjunct approach in HNSCC, particularly in chemoresistant settings.
authors: Rosy Iara Maciel de Azambuja Ribeiro

title: Vulvar High-Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion in Primary Lymphedema With Severe Genital Lymphorrhea: A Case Report.
abstract: Vulvar high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) is an HPV-associated premalignant lesion requiring prompt management. Its occurrence in primary lymphedema is rarely described. We report a 37-year-old woman with childhood-onset primary lymphedema who presented after 31 years of clinical quiescence with recurrent right lower-extremity and genital lymphedema presenting with vulvar swelling, erythema, follicular lesions, and persistent lymphorrhea. Indocyanine green (ICG) lymphography confirmed recurrent combined genital and lower-extremity lymphedema. Lymphaticovenular anastomosis (LVA) and abnormal perineal tissue excision were performed during the same operative session at different sites. Histopathology unexpectedly demonstrated multifocal vulvar HSIL with lymphangiectatic change. Immunohistochemistry showed p16 and Ki-67 overexpression, wild-type p53, D2-40 positivity, and CD34 negativity. HPV genotyping detected HPV16 and HPV42. Lymphorrhea decreased substantially, and leg volume decreased by 9.5%. Chronic genital lymphedema can obscure premalignant disease; morphologically abnormal or persistent vulvar lesions warrant histopathological assessment. LVA may reduce lymphorrhea and edema but cannot replace definitive oncologic treatment.
journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research

title: Cultural and structural barriers to HPV vaccine acceptance among young women in the United Arab Emirates
abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a common sexually transmitted virus, and oncogenic genotypes are linked to cervical cancer. Vaccination reduces cervical cancer burden, yet uptake remains suboptimal in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) despite national immunisation initiatives. This exploratory study aimed to identify and characterize potential cultural and structural barriers that may impede vaccine uptake among educated, digitally connected women in the UAE to inform future, more representative research. METHODS: A cross-sectional, descriptive study surveyed 1455 women aged 18-30 years across all emirates regarding vaccination status, cultural beliefs, and institutional factors influencing vaccine acceptance and uptake. RESULTS: The participants were predominantly educated, non-Emirati, digitally connected young women (mean age 22.4 years, 77.7% non-Emirati, 44.8% healthcare-affiliated). While 58.8% respondents viewed vaccination as culturally acceptable, only 26.2% admitted to being vaccinated. The most commonly reported barriers to vaccination included concerns about side effects, feeling too young for vaccination, and fear of family judgment (47.5%, 28.4%, 27.8%, respectively). The most reported reason for receiving the vaccine was its inclusion in the immunisation schedule (37.9%), followed by parental consent and encouragement (36.6%), and for self-protection purposes (25.6%). Furthermore, acceptance increased when the vaccine was presented as a cancer prevention strategy (64.6%), offered at more convenient location (63.8%) or made more affordable (61.5%). CONCLUSION: Overall, the primary barriers to vaccination included concerns regarding the fear of public judgment, reflecting a combination of informational gaps, timing-related considerations, and sociocultural influences affecting HPV vaccine uptake. Future research employing representative sampling is needed to determine whether these barriers generalize to broader UAE populations including non-digitally connected, non-healthcare workers, and Emirati women. Once population level barriers are identified through representative research, public health strategies can be designed to address context-appropriate concerns through targeted education on vaccine safety and culturally sensitive engagement with families and young women to improve uptake.

title: Sexually transmitted co-infections as biological modifiers of HPV-driven cervical carcinogenesis: a systematic integrative review
abstract: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection is necessary but not sufficient for cervical cancer, which caused approximately 350,000 deaths in 2022. Co-infections with Chlamydia trachomatis (CT), herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2), and HIV may modify cervical carcinogenesis, but causal inference is constrained by confounding, study heterogeneity, and limited mechanistic validation in human tissue. This systematic integrative review (PRISMA 2020) searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library (January 2015 to March 2026); risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and ROBINS-I, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. HIV co-infection shows the strongest evidence: approximately 6-fold risk elevation, a confirmed CD4 dose-response, and residual risk that persists despite antiretroviral therapy (GRADE: high). CT is associated with 2-4-fold elevations in observational studies, but substantial heterogeneity, residual sexual-behavior confounding, funnel-plot asymmetry suggesting publication bias, and attenuation of the HPV-adjusted independent effect (OR 1.76, 95% CI 1.03-3.01) leave causality uncertain (GRADE: Low-Moderate). HSV-2 associations are inconsistent: pooled cervical cancer risk was elevated (OR 3.01, 95% CI 2.24-4.04), but most estimates were unadjusted for HPV status, prospective studies are non-significant, and mechanistic evidence derives from non-human models (GRADE: low). A context-dependent syndemic effect appears in HIV co-infected populations. In conclusion, HIV meets criteria for a probable causal modifier of HPV-driven carcinogenesis, supporting WHO-endorsed intensified screening for women living with HIV; CT’s role remains uncertain pending rigorous confounder control; and HSV-2 does not meet the threshold for independent co-factor classification. Priorities include prospective cohorts and human cervical-tissue mechanistic validation.
journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

title: Trends in utilization of cervical cancer screening and screening-associated services in a multi-organizational research network in Chicago, Illinois, US.
abstract: PURPOSE: Chicago has a high degree of care fragmentation, with multiple large health systems and numerous safety-net systems. Fragmentation may be why the west and south areas of Chicago have high incidences of cervical cancer despite high self-reported screening rates. This study assesses utilization of cervical cancer screening-associated tests and procedures across seven health systems in Chicago between 2012 and 2022. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included females aged 15+ years enrolled in one or more health systems in the CAPriCORN network. Data were analyzed with descriptive statistics, geolocation, linear mixed-effects model, and Poisson regression. Proportions and trends in utilization by year of test modalities (cytology alone, cytology and human papillomavirus (HPV) test [cotest], HPV test alone, colposcopy, and cervical procedures [cone biopsy, loop electrosurgical excision procedure, and ablation]) were calculated and stratified by Chicago's six geographic zones. The time between screening utilization was compared by age, Chicago zone, and change in health system. RESULTS: Of 1.20 million in the study cohort, 53.6% had only 1 screening test during the 11-year study period; 22.9% had 2 tests, and 22.9% had 3 or more. Individuals in Chicago who changed health systems between two consecutive screening tests had a longer median interval between tests compared with those who did not change (34 versus 15.4 months). CONCLUSIONS: Over half of the cohort only had one screening test and may be underscreened. Switching health systems more than doubled the time interval between screening tests compared with patients who remained in the same system.

RESULTS: Of 1.20 million in the study cohort, 53.6% had only 1 screening test during the 11-year study period; 22.9% had 2 tests, and 22.9% had 3 or more. title: Modelling the expected and potentially preventable burden of infection-related cancer among newly arrived migrants in the European Union
abstract: International migration is rising globally. Newly arrived migrants (defined as individuals relocating into countries in the European Union) are a European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) priority population for entry health assessments--offering opportunities to prevent infection-related cancers but rarely implemented in practice. Using migration, cancer incidence, and intervention data, we modelled the burden of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), cervical cancer (CvC), and gastric cancer (GC) and the proportion potentially preventable by interventions: HBV vaccination, HBV and HCV screen-and-treat, HPV vaccination, cervical screening, and H. pylori screen-and-treat. We estimated 635,000 cancer cases over their lifetime (144,000 HCC, 155,000 CvC, 336,000 GC). Assuming full uptake, ECDC-recommended hepatitis interventions could prevent 15% of HCC cases; HPV vaccination and cervical screening could prevent 65% and 60% of CvC cases among eligible migrants, respectively; and H. pylori screen-and-treat could prevent 44% of GC cases among all migrants. Expanding eligibility could further increase impact.

title: From non-uptake during early adolescence to acceptance during a catch-up campaign: a qualitative study of changing HPV vaccination decisions across two life stages among young women in Amsterdam, the Netherlands
abstract: BackgroundHuman Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination effectively prevents HPV-related disease, but its population-level impact depends on sufficient coverage. In 2023-2024, the Netherlands offered free HPV vaccination to individuals aged 19-27 years through a national catch-up campaign. For women, this was a second opportunity, as they had been offered vaccination at ages 9-13 through the National Immunisation Programme (NIP). Back then, uptake was relatively low (46-57% in these birth cohorts), but uptake increased to 55-63% following the catch-up vaccination. This campaign provided an apt opportunity to explore the factors underlying previous and current HPV vaccination decisions among the same women across two life stages. MethodsBetween May 2023 and May 2024, 16 semi-structured interviews were conducted in Amsterdam with women who accepted HPV vaccination during the catch-up after non-uptake during early adolescence. Interviews explored factors influencing non-uptake and later acceptance, guided by the Health Belief Model and additional sociocultural constructs. Data were analysed using thematic analysis with open and theory-guided coding in MAXQDA. ResultsNon-uptake during early adolescence was primarily shaped by parental decision-making, cultural and religious norms, fear of side effects, low perceived susceptibility to HPV and limited self-efficacy. Acceptance in young adulthood was driven by greater autonomy, higher perceived susceptibility, increased trust in accumulated vaccine evidence and accessible vaccination infrastructure. Peer influence replaced parental influence as the dominant social factor. ConclusionHPV vaccine decision-making is a dynamic process rather than fixed. Permanent catch-up HPV vaccination opportunities would enable young adults to make autonomous vaccination decisions as their circumstances change. Highlights- Adolescent HPV non-uptake was driven by parents, culture and safety fears; - Adult acceptance was driven by perceived risk, greater trust and peer influence; - Decision-making is a dynamic state, not a fixed one-time decision; - Free, accessible infrastructures to vaccination enabled catch-up uptake; - Catch-up HPV vaccination enables autonomous vaccine decisions in young adults.

title: A parallel SEC Column configuration strategy for comprehensive characterization of HPV type 16 virus-like particles.
abstract: Characterisation of human papillomavirus-like particles (HPV VLPs) is challenging due to their large size and inherent structural heterogeneity. Monitoring oligomerisation of L1 proteins during VLP assembly is particularly difficult, as conventional large-pore-size exclusion chromatography (SEC) columns lack the resolving power to distinguish between L1 monomers and higher-order oligomers. This study presents an analytical approach utilizing two SEC columns with distinct pore sizes arranged in parallel, facilitating the separation of a wide range of molecular species within a single workflow. Hyphenation with multi-angle light scattering (MALS) provides the absolute molecular weight of the resolved species. Using the proposed parallel SEC column configuration, five distinct peaks were successfully resolved, compared to only two peaks with the 2000 Å column and three peaks with the 300 Å column, highlighting the enhanced separation capability for VLP species in 30 min, reducing both analysis time and sample consumption by up to 50% compared with performing two separate single-column analyses. This approach also simplifies the analytical workflow and lowers operational costs relative to more complex platforms such as 2D-LC systems. The proposed method was employed to characterise aggregates, monomeric VLPs, partially assembled VLPs and free L1 proteins in crude, purified and reassembled VLP samples. The proposed approach was validated using commercially available Gardasil HPV-VLP. Overall, the workflow enhances resolution across the size spectrum, provides accurate quantification of intact VLPs, reduces runtime and improves overall analytical throughput for VLP characterisation.

title: Understanding intravaginal practices for gynecologic health among Haitian migrant women: A mixed-methods analysis.
abstract: Haitian migrant women in the U.S. experience disproportionate rates of cervical cancer. Intravaginal practices (IVPs) are widely used among Haitian women and have been linked to an increased risk of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection. Although IVPs are well-documented in the Haitian community, little is known about Haitian migrant women’s perceptions and motivations underlying their use. This exploratory sequential mixed-methods study examined Haitian migrant women’s motivations for engaging in IVPs, products used for IVPs, and indications for their use. A convenience sample of Haitian migrant women in South Florida were recruited through active and passive recruitment approaches in community-based centers. Semi-structured qualitative interviews (n = 25) explored perceptions, motivations, and products used for IVPs. title: Comparison of self-sampling versus clinician-sampling HPV DNA cervical cancer screening in South African women living with and without HIV.
abstract: Abstract Introduction Human papilloma virus (HPV) testing is the preferred primary screening method for cervical cancer, and HPV self‐sampling has the potential to improve screening uptake. We compared the test performance and agreement of self‐ and clinician‐sampling HPV in women living with HIV (WLWH) and HIV‐negative women in Gauteng and Western Cape Province, South Africa. Methods Cervical cancer screening was performed in previously unscreened women using cytology, self‐ and clinician‐collected HPV (Hybrid Capture 2 assay). Screen‐positive participants underwent colposcopy and biopsy, and a random sample of negative screens had punch biopsy regardless of colposcopy findings. Performances of screening tests were evaluated against histology results adjusted for verification bias. The kappa statistic for HPV concordance between self‐ and clinician‐collected HPV was also calculated. Results Included for analysis were 903 women with a mean age of 41.5 years, of which 43.3% were WLWH. In WLWH/HIV‐negative women, the sensitivity of self‐sampling HPV was 74.7%/67.4% and of clinician‐sampling HPV was 77.1%/59.2% to detect cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) grade3+, whereas the specificity for clinician‐sampling HPV was 75.0%/86.8% compared with 70.3%/79.8% for self‐sampling HPV to detect CIN2+. In both HIV groups, Cohen's kappa agreement between the two sampling methods was good (0.63 and 0.62, respectively). Conclusion Self‐collected HPV sampling is an acceptable and viable option for primary cervical cancer screening in all women given the superior sensitivity to cytology. The statistically significant difference in HPV test performance among HIV‐negative women according to sampling method confirms the benefit of a further triage test when self‐sampling is used for HPV‐base cervical screening, especially in HIV‐negative women.

title: Strengthening Prevention and Awareness of HPV-Related Oropharyngeal Cancers Through Partnership with Regional Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Services
abstract: This commentary highlights community priorities from a longitudinal cohort study addressing human papillomavirus-related oropharyngeal cancer prevention and awareness among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples in South Australia. Spanning eight years, the project aims to explore the prevalence, incidence and persistence of human papillomavirus, with future research directions strengthened by longstanding partnership and input between researchers and Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Organisations. Through reflections from this partnership, we highlight the current state of human papillomavirus and cancer awareness in communities including: (i) community access to dental care and mouth cancer screening; (ii) sexual health awareness, knowledge, and education; and (iii) community awareness around cancer. We state key priorities to be actioned in the next phase of this research including: (i) incorporating culturally safe education and awareness alongside identifying high-risk human papillomavirus prevalence; (ii) community outreach and engagement activities; and (iii) Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander workforce training, education and empowerment. Embedding these priorities are essential to advancing equitable oral cancer prevention and ensuring that Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities are not overlooked in existing health promotion efforts.

title: Vaccination-driven suppression, stochastic variability, and contact saturation in HPV-cervical cancer transmission in India: A Black-Karasinski perturbation model.
abstract: This study develops two stochastic models (one representing the pre-vaccination era and the other representing the vaccination era) describing human papillomavirus infection and its progression to cervical cancer in India. Both models incorporate Holling type-II incidence, with transmission dynamics perturbed by the Black-Karasinski stochastic process. A rigorous theoretical analysis is conducted for these models. The existence and uniqueness of global positive solutions are established, followed by the derivation of threshold quantities governing persistence and extinction. When R i s >1(i=1,2), each model admits at least one stationary distribution, indicating long-term persistence of infection. In contrast, when R i e <1(i=1,2), the infection undergoes exponential extinction. The non-vaccination model is fitted to annual cervical cancer incidence data from India for the period 2003 to 2017. Substituting the fitted parameter values within the specified time horizon implies that the system remains persistent under the current conditions. Subsequently, for the vaccination model, the remaining parameters are estimated from reliable scientific data, and simulations are carried out from 2025 onward. For the vaccination period, the estimated parameter values indicate eventual eradication of infection. Extensive numerical simulations support the theoretical findings. A global sensitivity analysis using Latin hypercube sampling and partial rank correlation coefficients identifies the most influential parameters. Finally, extinction time distributions and survival probabilities are examined to provide policy-relevant insights toward achieving an HPV-free India within the next 50 years.
